correctness.rationale: The theorem holds for all \(n\ge4\): the support-union map and full-two-subset section are a genuine \(S_n\)-equivariant poset equivalence. The rank-selected Boolean complex is induced in a barycentrically subdivided sphere of dimension \(n-2\); its complement retracts equivariantly onto the deleted singleton/co-singleton crown graph. Alexander duality has an integral orientation-sign twist. The connected crown graph has cochain differential giving exactly the row/column sublattice of rank \(2n-1\), a unimodular spanning-tree minor and torsion-free quotient of rank \(n^2-3n+1\). Other reduced cohomology vanishes. Field coefficients follow by universal coefficients. Independent direct-neighborhood and Boolean-poset fixed-chain trace calculations agree for all permutations on four, five, and six letters and four permutations on seven letters; these tests corroborate, but do not replace, the general proof.

originality.rationale: The sole accepted novelty is a uniform, explicit integral \(\mathbb Z[S_n]\)-lattice isomorphism to sign-twisted crown-graph cohomology. The 2018 wedge count and the rational ribbon/Specht character already follow from prior results and are expressly excluded. The close six-point published RESULT.md was inspected and addresses only a rational specialization, explicitly disclaiming integral classification. No inspected source supplies the row/column integral identification. An unindexed or indirectly derivable equivalent integral result remains a genuine originality risk.
residual_risks: A published but unindexed explicit integral crown-graph lattice representation may exist.
Earlier Boolean-lattice integral Specht lattice literature might indirectly identify the same module, beyond the characteristic-zero result checked.
The 2026 general paper was inspected in its relevant sections rather than every line of all 59 pages; the relevant broader complex module is acknowledged as covered.

value.rationale: The exact natural \(\mathbb Z[S_n]\)-module is a motivated equivariant invariant of the Lovász neighborhood construction. A complete integral row/column incidence quotient gives modular representations for every prime, including nonsemisimple characteristics, which rational ranks and semisimple Specht decompositions cannot uniquely determine. The crown dual graph and Alexander-duality sign give explicit structural information rather than arbitrary numerical slices. The known nonequivariant wedge type and rational character are excluded from novelty.
